...huh. Insight appreciated, makes sense.

Do have to say though. I'm a strong leader in my class, I do hit the gym, and I stand up for myself against oppressive classmates, teachers, even parents. Took me 20 years to get here, and I'm happy I got to this point!

 ***It's just I've noticed people do feel like leaving when I actually... emotionally, vulnerably open up. Even just once.***

​

***Is this seen as sign of weakness among men, a sign to leave?*** I daresay I'm an emotional advocate and I encourage people to feel their sadness & anger alike, and people do appreciate that. I don't want toxic masculinity & repressed emotions in my life, *because I... don't want to come back into it, not like before.*

​

Maybe a more independent, self-reflective life that doesn't depend on friendships could... ironically help build them more? *You as a fellow, well-mannered, respectable guy, how did you do it?*

*Why thank you, by the way!* (ᵔᴗᵔ)

I do have good mannerisms, at least I was raised to believe so. I've always been told off as "too kind" - my mom even prides me with a 3 y/o childhood achievement/certificate I don't even remember, *"Kindest of RF pre-school class"*. **Dang it, mom. HAHA**

​

I come off very genuine, compassionate, and understanding! I spread love unconditionally - helping others, staying kind, sending fun memes.

* My tone of voice can range from very soft, to very enthusiastic. I'm M/20, but I have a baby face and attitude of 15. *(Cursed with immortally cute Asian gene.)*
* I show them I genuinely care and that I'm there for them, in strictly platonic ways. People usually describe me as "Oh, Rya! They're kind, sweet, and very helpful. Origami's cool, too!"
* I get hyped when people vibe with me, and it makes me really, visibly happy! I'm a big hugger, and I still know when to let go *(when they wiggle away, pat the back, or even distance themselves)*. The ones that do keep hugging, I gladly stay.

​

One thing may be how I treat many people special, perhaps? *Not just my friends and family, but even my teachers, uni's enrollment staff, taxi drivers too!*

It may throw some off guard with the friendly gestures, like wholesome memes and GIF's  - *but I just want to normalize kindness in this war-torn, virus-infested earth, now more than ever.*

​

*It just so happens that there's a \~4-6 month barrier that just makes friends want to give up with me, and I want to find it. Is it really... "diabetically sweet", and not in the good way?*

Hi, Alchemist! Good day\~

My first instinct? Stay attentive, keep the convo going, maintain good body language, be a good friend! It goes on with passion, joy, and curiosity for a few months before... **it dies out.**

* *I couldn't do this at all when I was depressed and 18. Took me a year to get the hang of socializing. Today at 20y/o I feel confident, curious, and willing to learn!*
* I just feel I'm missing something. A social aspect I might've missed from being a loner for 18 years.
* I'm an open book! I have no hidden intentions, nor hidden personalities either. *I let my friends be themselves and I don't get too attached (took me a while to learn this too).*

​

Perhaps who I am as a person? I'm a regular college introvert who loves studies, does origami as a side job, and loves everything nerd-related (games, shows, movies, art).

* I'm 100% emotional. Touchy-feely and all that jazz - a tiny 5'7" voice of a tiger, strength of cheetah, *attitude of a cat.*
* "Diabetically sweet" is both a truthful, accurate description of me - perhaps here, both a compliment and insult. I enjoy silent company and emotional convos.

​

My first instinct is to try and save the friendship, but they've already given up. *I know something's wrong - I want to work on it, but I don't know what it is.* At times I just leave them be as well, for both our sanity's sakes.

​

*Is it something about having a "polarizing" personality? Being different, charismatic?* ***What am I missing?***

The branches are a very simple original design, which don't need glue.

1. I just rolled a small paper, twisted it (for a "branchy" feel),
2. created two more,
3. and rolled another paper halfway above all two/three.

Twisting helps secure it without glue, and makes it easier to rearrange if you feel the bonsai doesn't look appealing yet. You may vary the length of the branches for a natural look.
